Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

information noun

also inform, let me know, be informed, info

classical

Cic. Fam. 2.4.1
Cael. in Cic. Fam. 8.1.1: fac mē certiōrem

certiōrem facere

phrase: certus in the comparative with faciō

to inform someone, give him information; certior fierī, to be informed

Latin gives information with a verb: fac mē certiōrem, let me know; certior factus sum, I have been told. The thing goes with dē.

Other words

  • indicium, indiciī n. — information given, a disclosure, a tip-off

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Plaut. Cist. 4.2.9: facite indicium, sī quis vīdit (Lewis & Short); Ter. Ad. 4.4.7: id anus mihi indicium fēcit (Lewis & Short); Traupman 217, 333

    Often of information laid against someone (Caes. BG 1.4).

  • nūntius, nūntiī m. — news, a message; a messenger

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Catull. 9.5: ō mihi nūntiī beātī!

  • cognitiō, cognitiōnis f. — knowledge, finding out about a thing

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · M-O s.v. information: ūnicum fontem cognitiōnis nostrae, our only source of information (Sillig)

  • īnfōrmātiō, īnfōrmātiōnis f. — an outline; an idea, a notion

    noun, third declension · avoid · classical · Cic. ND 1.43: anteceptam animō reī quandam īnfōrmātiōnem

    A false friend: classically a sketch (Vitruvius) or an idea formed in the mind. Morgan–Owens allows it for the act of informing (Thunberg 1784), not for information as facts.

Examples

  • ut certiōrēs facerēmus absentīs, sī quid esset quod eōs scīre aut nostrā aut ipsōrum interesset

    to tell those far away anything that it mattered to us, or to them, that they should knowCic. Fam. 2.4.1

  • fac mē certiōrem

    let me knowCael. in Cic. Fam. 8.1.1

See also interest, learn.
